principle: Course order is explicit. Existing paths remain stable.

stages.title: Open, save and find your work
stages.activity: No prior knowledge. Follow its eight lessons in order.
stages.readiness: You can create a folder, recognise a file, and explain input, instructions and output.

stages.title: Read and write a small program
stages.activity: Complete First programs, then Working with more information.
stages.readiness: You can explain values, decisions, loops, functions, arrays, a pointer and the difference between a declaration and a definition.

stages.title: Keep a history of changes
stages.activity: Use a practice folder after learning to edit and save files.
stages.readiness: You can describe a local change and a recorded snapshot without discarding work.

stages.title: Build a small Framework application
stages.activity: Learn the Framework introduction, CMake, SDK use and shared activity rule as one project.
stages.readiness: You can distinguish configure, build, test and run, and trace one call from its declaration to its result.

stages.title: Give the same program a window
stages.activity: Continue with the same activity-counter project.
stages.readiness: You can explain a widget, a signal and a callback, and identify the shared rule used by the window and console.

stages.title: Change a feature and investigate a failure
stages.activity: Change one rule in your own practice copy; compare expected and observed results.
stages.readiness: You can reproduce a problem, identify the responsible function and explain the check that should catch it.

stages.title: Extend a shared service
stages.activity: Continue after the first application and diagnostic exercises.
stages.readiness: You can separate reusable behaviour in Framework from application presentation, then choose one specialist topic.

subjects.title: 1. Computers and first programs
subjects.before: No previous computing or programming knowledge.
subjects.outcome: Find a saved file, follow a command, and explain a small program.

courses.title: Introduction to Computers
courses.purpose: Start here. Learn files, folders, instructions, memory and commands through eight introductory lessons.

courses.title: Learning C
courses.purpose: Continue with First programs, then Working with more information. Leave systems studies until later.

courses.title: Introduction to Version Control
courses.purpose: After editing and saving files, learn how to record and review changes.

subjects.title: 2. Building Umicom applications
subjects.before: C variables, decisions, loops, functions, arrays, pointers and separate source files.
subjects.outcome: Understand one small Framework application from source to a tested console program and a GTK4 window.

courses.title: Learning Visual Studio for Umicom development
courses.purpose: Optional development-tool guide: open real source, keep the repository toolchain, build, test and inspect a program. No completed Umicom Studio installation is required.

courses.title: Umicom Framework Development
courses.purpose: Follow the introductory project first. Choose the later source studies only after completing it.

courses.title: Building a Web Server in C
courses.purpose: A later project: requests, handlers and lifetime after C and Framework foundations.

courses.title: Learning GTK4
courses.purpose: Build a small event-driven window and trace its connection to a shared rule.

subjects.title: 3. Web development
subjects.before: Files and folders. Learn HTML before CSS, and both before browser JavaScript.
subjects.outcome: Read the task-board example as a page, its presentation and its behaviour.

courses.title: Learning HTML
courses.purpose: Begin with meaningful page structure, links and images.

courses.title: Learning CSS
courses.purpose: Style an HTML page, then check resizing and keyboard access.

courses.title: Learning JavaScript
courses.purpose: Add events and visible state to the page; then examine local storage.

courses.title: Learning PHP
courses.purpose: Continue on the server after learning forms, requests and basic programming.

courses.title: Learning SQL
courses.purpose: Store and query a small learning catalogue, then group changes safely.

courses.title: Learning Bootstrap
courses.purpose: Use a CSS toolkit while retaining semantic HTML and accessible controls.

courses.title: Learning React
courses.purpose: Describe reusable views and connect deliberate events to visible state.

courses.title: Learning Zend Framework
courses.purpose: Understand the Zend Framework heritage and practise focused components through Laminas.

courses.title: Learning Laravel
courses.purpose: Follow a web request through a route into an escaped lesson view.

courses.title: Learning CodeIgniter
courses.purpose: Build a small explicitly routed page and understand controller/view responsibilities.

courses.title: Learning Spring Framework
courses.purpose: Follow Java web requests and supply shared dependencies explicitly.

subjects.title: 4. Other programming languages
subjects.before: Some programming experience helps with the current code-study chapters. Return to Learning C for a fuller introduction to variables, functions and control flow.
subjects.outcome: Compare how existing note and journal examples express similar operations in another language.

courses.title: Learning Python
courses.purpose: Introductory code studies of a notes example, followed by JSON and file errors.

courses.title: Learning C++
courses.purpose: After C, study objects and resource lifetime through a note journal.

courses.title: Learning Java
courses.purpose: Study records, a journal and decimal calculations. These are initial chapters, not a complete language course.

courses.title: Learning Rust
courses.purpose: Explore typed values and borrowing while comparing ownership with C contracts.

courses.title: Learning Zig
courses.purpose: Read typed operations and explicit error results with small Zig tests.

courses.title: Learning Kotlin
courses.purpose: Write and check a small lesson-progress program. Start with installing a JDK and the Kotlin compiler, then create a file, compile it and explain its values and functions.

courses.title: Learning D Language
courses.purpose: Create a native program with the D compiler. Learn how source becomes an executable, then check a function with input validation and unit tests.

subjects.title: 5. Systems, processors and compilers
subjects.before: Complete C foundations and the further systems studies. Understand memory, bytes, pointers, functions and build tools.
subjects.outcome: Trace real system boundaries and carry out a small, separately documented experiment.

courses.title: Introduction to RISC-V
courses.purpose: Learn registers, memory and privilege before Assembly source studies.

courses.title: Learning RISC-V Assembly
courses.purpose: Follow calls, returns and interrupted registers using Kernel examples.

courses.title: Umicom Kernel from Scratch
courses.purpose: A specialist route through hosted checks and native Kernel code. Read each lab prerequisite first.

courses.title: Umicom OS from Scratch
courses.purpose: A parallel systems route: startup, services, recovery and image evidence.

courses.title: Building a Compiler in C
courses.purpose: A separate project using Umicom C: source, tokens, expressions, execution and diagnostics.

courses.title: Learning x86 Assembly
courses.purpose: Trace registers and a small x86-64 function before attempting platform-specific programs.

courses.title: Learning Motorola 68000 Assembly
courses.purpose: Trace registers, bytes in memory and bounded loops using short MC68000 examples and related C exercises.

courses.title: Learning Motorola 6800 Assembly
courses.purpose: Understand an 8-bit processor through accumulator, memory and branch traces.

courses.title: Learning Linux Development
courses.purpose: Build and inspect a small user-space program before exploring operating-system services.

courses.title: Building Linux from Scratch Using C Code
courses.purpose: Understand the path from a hosted C program to a Linux system, then plan an isolated source-build environment. C examples explain components; building Linux also requires toolchains, scripts, packages and configuration.

subjects.title: 6. Mathematics and AI
subjects.before: Start with the mathematics course. For programming chapters, also complete C foundations and build tools.
subjects.outcome: Explain a small model, inspect its native implementation and distinguish training from evaluation.

courses.title: Mathematics for AI
courses.purpose: Build mathematical foundations before model internals.

courses.title: Building an LLM from Scratch
courses.purpose: Learn the model pipeline before choosing advanced native source studies.

courses.title: Introduction to Distributed Learning
courses.purpose: After one model and its training loop, study workers, communication and verification.

courses.title: Guide to AI Research
courses.purpose: Further reading after the model course; research topics are not prerequisites for a first program.

courses.title: Native Local AI Chat and Media with Umicom Framework
courses.purpose: Connect native Framework services to local chat and plan grounded, governed image/video workflows.

subjects.title: 7. Financial systems and ledgers
subjects.before: Begin with the business and financial lessons. C and Framework knowledge are needed for the software exercises.
subjects.outcome: Follow fictional accounts, trades and payments through explicit rules and records.

courses.title: Umicom application and financial-system studies
courses.purpose: Choose the software or financial route inside this collection. They are separate subjects, not a single beginner course.

courses.title: Introduction to Blockchain and Distributed Ledgers
courses.purpose: Study records and validation first, then choose the later consensus and implementation topics.

courses.title: Introduction to Treasury Management Systems
courses.purpose: Understand cash, commitments and the evidence a treasury system must keep.

courses.title: Learning Pine Script
courses.purpose: Read chart series, create a small indicator and understand when chart values become final.

courses.title: Financial Instruments Pricing Using C, C++ and Java
courses.purpose: Learn to describe a financial contract, calculate its cashflows, implement the same calculation in three languages and trace reusable pricing into Umicom Framework.

courses.title: Introduction to Bitcoin
courses.purpose: Understand payments, spendable outputs, signatures and competing histories before reading code or attempting an implementation.

courses.title: Introduction to Bitcoin Source Code
courses.purpose: Read a fixed Bitcoin Core source release using a responsibility map, then trace a transaction check without mistaking one function for the whole protocol.

courses.title: Introduction to Blockchain
courses.purpose: Learn what a ledger records, why hashes link records and which problems require agreement between independent participants.

courses.title: Building Blockchain from Scratch
courses.purpose: Construct a small offline ledger step by step: exact record bytes, validation, state changes and recoverable storage. Reuse Framework services when integrating the teaching design.

courses.title: Building Bitcoin from Scratch Using Assembly and C
courses.purpose: Build carefully bounded Bitcoin-format learning components in C and study where Assembly can help. Start offline, with explicit compatibility checks and no real keys or funds.

courses.title: Introduction to Calypso API Development
courses.purpose: Learn service boundaries, Java adapter design and controlled integration exercises using Umicom treasury training material. Vendor-specific compilation requires the matching licensed SDK.

subjects.title: Earlier course editions
subjects.before: These addresses remain available for existing bookmarks. New learners should use the foundation route above.
subjects.outcome: Revisit an earlier reading sequence without repeating it as a new prerequisite.

courses.title: Introduction to Computers — earlier course address
courses.purpose: Preserved alongside the current Introduction to Computers course.

courses.title: Learning C — earlier reading sequence
courses.purpose: Preserved alongside Learning C. It is not an additional course you must complete.

subjects.title: Mobile application development
subjects.before: No earlier course is required. Each course explains its tools and first example.
subjects.outcome: Run a small application, connect a button to visible state and check its behaviour.

courses.title: Android Development
courses.purpose: Build a small lesson counter for an Android device or emulator. Begin with the development tools, run the generated application, then connect a button to visible screen state.

courses.title: Learning Flutter
courses.purpose: Create a small lesson counter using Dart and Flutter. Begin by running the generated project, then learn widgets, state, callbacks and automated interaction checks.

subjects.title: Development environments (optional)
subjects.before: Find files, save text and open PowerShell. No model-training or Python-programming experience is required.
subjects.outcome: Select and inspect an isolated Python environment without changing the supported native toolchain.

courses.title: Conda and Miniforge for Umicom Developers
courses.purpose: Ten ordered lessons, a command reference and an environment-isolation capstone. Practical commands are unexecuted teaching examples.
